concept_en: A Knight on a Weak-Square Outpost
question_cn: 为什么「马占弱格」是弱格利用中最理想的方式之一？
question_en: Why is placing a knight on a weak square one of the best ways to exploit it?

options.text_cn: 马在任何格子都同样强大，与弱格无关
options.text_en: A knight is equally strong on every square, regardless of weaknesses.

options.text_cn: 马在弱格上无法被对方兵驱走，若对方又缺乏同色象，则马稳如泰山，成为永久据点
options.text_en: An enemy pawn cannot drive the knight away from a weak square; without a matching bishop, the knight can become a permanent outpost.

options.text_cn: 马比象强大，占据任何中心格都有优势
options.text_en: Knights are stronger than bishops, so any central square is an advantage.

options.text_cn: 马在弱格上主要是为了防守，阻止对方进攻
options.text_en: A knight on a weak square is mainly defensive and stops attacks.

explanation_cn: 弱格的本质是「兵无法保护」，而驱走棋子最便宜的方式正是用兵。马占据弱格后，对方没有兵能斜向攻击驱走它，若对方恰好失去了该颜色的象，连「用象换马」的选项都没有。这样的马被称为「永久据点马」（Outpost Knight），它控制的格子范围广，对中残局有决定性影响。尼姆佐印度和国王印度中都有经典的Nd5/Nd4据点马案例。
explanation_en: A weak square cannot be protected by a pawn, and pawns are often the cheapest way to drive away an enemy piece. A knight on such a square cannot be chased by a pawn; if the opponent has also lost the bishop of that color, even a bishop-for-knight exchange may be unavailable. This permanent outpost knight can control many squares and have a major impact in the middlegame and endgame.
